evidence_text: The CAPM is a model for pricing an individual security or portfolio. For individual securities, it makes use of the security market line (SML)
logical_form: if CAPM uses SML for individual securities, then CAPM is a model for pricing an individual security or portfolio

evidence_text: For individual securities, it makes use of the security market line (SML) and its relation to expected return and systematic risk (beta) to show how the market must price individual securities in relation to their security risk class. The SML enables us to calculate the reward-to-risk ratio for any security in relation to that of the overall market.
logical_form: if SML is used to price individual securities, then SML enables calculation of reward-to-risk ratio

evidence_text: The SML enables us to calculate the reward-to-risk ratio for any security in relation to that of the overall market. When the expected rate of return for any security is deflated by its beta coefficient, the reward-to-risk ratio for any individual security in the market is equal to the market reward-to-risk ratio.
logical_form: if reward-to-risk ratio can be calculated, then deflating expected return by beta equals market reward-to-risk ratio

evidence_text: For individual securities, it makes use of the security market line (SML) and its relation to expected return and systematic risk (beta) to show how the market must price individual securities in relation to their security risk class. In equilibrium, all assets should plot directly on the SML.
logical_form: if CAPM uses SML, then in equilibrium all assets plot on SML

evidence_text: In equilibrium, all assets should plot directly on the SML. An asset located above the line is considered undervalued, as it offers a higher return for its level of systematic risk, while an asset below is overvalued.
logical_form: if assets plot on SML, then assets above the line are undervalued and assets below are overvalued

evidence_text: An asset located above the line is considered undervalued, as it offers a higher return for its level of systematic risk, while an asset below is overvalued. An asset located below is overvalued.

evidence_text: For individual securities, it makes use of the security market line (SML) and its relation to expected return and systematic risk (beta) to show how the market must price individual securities in relation to their security risk class. The slope of the SML represents the market risk premium, illustrating the trade-off between risk and return.
logical_form: if CAPM uses SML, then slope of SML represents market risk premium

evidence_text: For individual securities, it makes use of the security market line (SML) and its relation to expected return and systematic risk (beta) to show how the market must price individual securities in relation to their security risk class. evidence_text: The risk of a portfolio comprises systematic risk, also known as undiversifiable risk, and unsystematic risk, which is also known as idiosyncratic risk or diversifiable risk. Systematic risk refers to the risk common to all securities—i.e., market risk.
logical_form: if systematic risk is market risk, then portfolio risk comprises systematic and unsystematic risk

evidence_text: The risk of a portfolio comprises systematic risk, also known as undiversifiable risk, and unsystematic risk, which is also known as idiosyncratic risk or diversifiable risk. Unsystematic risk is the risk associated with individual assets.
logical_form: if unsystematic risk is risk associated with individual assets, then portfolio risk comprises systematic and unsystematic risk

evidence_text: Unsystematic risk is the risk associated with individual assets. Unsystematic risk can be diversified away to smaller levels by including a greater number of assets in the portfolio as specific risks "average out".
logical_form: if unsystematic risk is associated with individual assets, then including more assets diversifies away unsystematic risk
mechanism: Adding more assets to a portfolio reduces the impact of any single asset's specific risk, causing the overall unsystematic risk to decrease.

evidence_text: Unsystematic risk can be diversified away to smaller levels by including a greater number of assets in the portfolio as specific risks "average out". The same is not possible for systematic risk within one market.
logical_form: if unsystematic risk can be diversified, then systematic risk cannot be diversified
mechanism: Systematic risk affects all assets in the market, so increasing the number of assets in a portfolio does not reduce the overall exposure to systematic risk.

evidence_text: Unsystematic risk can be diversified away to smaller levels by including a greater number of assets in the portfolio as specific risks "average out". A portfolio of approximately 30–40 securities in developed markets such as the UK or US will render the portfolio sufficiently diversified such that risk exposure is limited to systematic risk only.
logical_form: if unsystematic risk can be diversified, then a portfolio of 30-40 securities limits risk exposure to systematic risk
mechanism: Adding 30-40 securities in developed markets diversifies away enough unsystematic risk to limit risk exposure to systematic risk.

evidence_text: A portfolio of approximately 30–40 securities in developed markets such as the UK or US will render the portfolio sufficiently diversified such that risk exposure is limited to systematic risk only. This number may vary depending on the way securities are weighted in a portfolio which alters the overall risk contribution of each security.
logical_form: if 30-40 securities diversifies risk, then the number may vary depending on security weighting
mechanism: The weighting of securities in a portfolio affects the overall risk contribution of each security, which can alter the number of securities needed for diversification.

evidence_text: This number may vary depending on the way securities are weighted in a portfolio which alters the overall risk contribution of each security. Market cap weighting means that securities of companies with larger market capitalization will take up a larger portion of the portfolio, making it effectively less diversified.
logical_form: if security weighting alters risk contribution, then market cap weighting makes portfolio less diversified
mechanism: Market cap weighting concentrates the portfolio in larger companies, reducing diversification and increasing the impact of those companies' performance on the portfolio.

evidence_text: A portfolio of approximately 30–40 securities in developed markets such as the UK or US will render the portfolio sufficiently diversified such that risk exposure is limited to systematic risk only. In developing markets, a larger number of securities is required for diversification due to higher asset volatilities.
logical_form: if 30-40 securities diversifies risk in developed markets, then a larger number is required in developing markets
mechanism: Higher asset volatilities in developing markets require a larger number of securities to achieve the same level of diversification as in developed markets.

evidence_text: The risk of a portfolio comprises systematic risk, also known as undiversifiable risk, and unsystematic risk, which is also known as idiosyncratic risk or diversifiable risk. A rational investor should not take on any diversifiable risk, as only non-diversifiable risks are rewarded within the scope of this model.
logical_form: if portfolio risk comprises systematic and unsystematic risk, then a rational investor should not take on diversifiable risk

evidence_text: A rational investor should not take on any diversifiable risk, as only non-diversifiable risks are rewarded within the scope of this model. Therefore, the required return on an asset must be linked to its contribution to overall portfolio riskiness as opposed to its "stand alone risk".
logical_form: if only non-diversifiable risks are rewarded, then required return must be linked to contribution to portfolio riskiness

evidence_text: Therefore, the required return on an asset must be linked to its contribution to overall portfolio riskiness as opposed to its "stand alone risk". In the CAPM context, portfolio risk is represented by higher variance—i.e., less predictability.
logical_form: if required return is linked to portfolio riskiness, then portfolio risk is represented by higher variance

evidence_text: In the CAPM context, portfolio risk is represented by higher variance—i.e., less predictability. In other words, the beta of the portfolio is the defining factor in rewarding the systematic exposure taken by an investor.
logical_form: if portfolio risk is higher variance, then beta is the defining factor in rewarding systematic exposure
